[Intro: loping bass line, light drums, gliding strings]

[Verse 1: laid-back lead, the band answers in brackets]
Hey (hey)
Who told you that you had to change? (yeah)

You don't have to earn a chair (yeah)
Hey (hey)
There was always one right there (ooh)

You were fine

[Chorus: easy groove, strings, group vocals]
Nothing wrong with you
Nothing wrong with you

[Instrumental: electric sitar-like guitar melody over the groove]

[Bridge: group chanting, handclaps]
Come on in, come on in
(Nothing wrong)
Come on in, come on in
(Nothing wrong)

[Final Chorus: everyone, strings soaring, ad-libs]
Nothing wrong with you
Nothing wrong with you
Bring what you've got, bring what you've been
Door's wide open, come on in
Nothing wrong with you

[Outro: bass line and strings, voices fading]
You were fine
You were fine
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 106 BPM, 4/4, D major. A loping, rolling, unhurried groove. Warm, loose and completely at ease.

VOICE: Male, relaxed and slightly nasal, with a drawl that sits just behind the beat. He calls out short lines and the rest of the band answers in a loose group. Group vocals on the chorus, and a chant in the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A round, loping electric bass line that carries the tune. A light, swinging drum kit. A string section playing long, gliding lines. A guitar with a twangy, sitar-like tone playing the instrumental melody. Clean rhythm guitar. Congas and handclaps.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, bass, drums and strings. 0:14 Verse 1. 0:40 Chorus 1. 1:02 Verse 2. 1:28 Chorus 2. 1:50 Instrumental with the sitar-like guitar. 2:12 Bridge, chant and claps. 2:30 Final chorus. 2:52 Outro, the bass and strings with voices fading by 3:15.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1970s West Coast pop-soul: warm, round and uncluttered, bass and strings forward, everything sitting back in the pocket.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first shouted 'Hey' and the band's reply at 0:14.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: 'You were fine before they told you' is the line of someone who has watched younger people be talked out of themselves. The song is advice from an elder with no lecture in it.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Reassurance, welcome, ease.
